properties.name: Cholera, Haiti
properties.agent: Vibrio cholerae O1, El Tor, Ogawa
properties.count_note: Suspected cases and deaths, October 2010 - February 2019 (WHO). Haiti's ministry: 819,786 cases, 9,789 deaths to December 2018.
properties.water: The first hospitalised patients lived in Meille, beside a UN peacekeeping camp built above a stream that flows into the Artibonite River; sewage from the camp reached the stream. Cases then exploded downstream in the Artibonite delta and coastal plain, among people who drank river water.
properties.sources: [["Piarroux et al. 2011, Emerging Infectious Diseases 17(7)", "https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/eid/article/17/7/11-0059"], ["WHO Disease Outbreak News, Haiti, 2022", "https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2022-DON415"]]

properties.name: Cholera, Zimbabwe
properties.count_note: Reported to the end of July 2009 (Mukandavire et al., PNAS 2011). Other tallies give up to 4,369 deaths.
properties.water: First cases reported on 20 August 2008. Broken water supply and overflowing sewers in a crowded town with chronic water shortages; it spread to all provinces.
properties.place: Chitungwiza (St Mary's and Zengeza wards), near Harare

properties.name: Cholera, Yemen
properties.count_note: Suspected cases and deaths to March 2021 (WHO EMRO); one of the largest cholera outbreaks ever recorded. 2021-2022 added fewer than 40,000 suspected cases.
properties.water: War-damaged water and sewage networks; the outbreak peaked in 2017.
properties.sources: [["WHO EMRO cholera situation reports", "https://applications.emro.who.int/docs/WHOEMCSR433E-eng.pdf"], ["WHO EMRO weekly update, December 2016", "https://www.emro.who.int/pandemic-epidemic-diseases/cholera/weekly-update-cholera-cases-in-yemen.html"]]

properties.name: Cholera, Malawi
properties.count_note: Cumulative to 7 April 2024 (WHO); Malawi's worst cholera outbreak in decades. Case fatality 3.0 %.
properties.water: First case registered in Machinga District on 2 March 2022; by mid-2023 all 29 districts had reported cases.
properties.sources: [["WHO Disease Outbreak News, Malawi, 2022", "https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2022-DON435"], ["WHO AFRO, Malawi", "https://www.afro.who.int/countries/malawi/news/malawi-launches-national-end-cholera-campaign"]]

properties.name: Cholera returns to the Americas, Peru
properties.agent: Vibrio cholerae O1, El Tor, Inaba
properties.count_note: All of the Americas to 28 August 1991 (PAHO); most cases were in Peru.
properties.water: The first cholera epidemic in South America in the 20th century. It ran along about 2,000 km of the populated coast within two weeks, through untreated drinking water and food.
properties.sources: [["CDC MMWR, Cholera - Peru, 1991", "https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/00001912.htm"], ["PAHO Bulletin special report, 1991", "https://es.ircwash.org/sites/default/files/SpecialReport-1991-Cholera.pdf"]]

properties.name: Cryptosporidium, Milwaukee
properties.count_note: About 403,000 people fell ill (MacKenzie et al., NEJM 1994). Reported deaths range from 69 to over 100 immunocompromised people, depending on the study.
properties.water: The largest documented waterborne outbreak in US history. Oocysts passed the plant's filters; the most likely source was sewage reaching its Lake Michigan intake, but the cause was never officially confirmed.
properties.place: Howard Avenue water treatment plant (Lake Michigan intake)

properties.name: E. coli O157:H7, Walkerton
properties.agent: E. coli O157:H7 and Campylobacter jejuni
properties.water: Heavy rain on 8-12 May 2000 washed cattle manure from a nearby farm into a shallow town well; continuous chlorine and turbidity monitoring would have prevented it (O'Connor inquiry).
properties.sources: [["Report of the Walkerton Inquiry, Part 1 summary", "https://www.archives.gov.on.ca/en/e_records/walkerton/report1/pdf/WI_Summary.pdf"]]

properties.name: Cyanide spill, Baia Mare
properties.count_note: 50-100 t of cyanide released; about 1,240 t of fish killed in Hungary.
properties.water: Through the Lapus, Somes and Tisza into the Danube; still measurable in the Danube delta about four weeks later.
properties.place: Aurul tailings dam, Baia Mare, Romania
properties.sources: [["UNEP/OCHA assessment mission, Cyanide spill at Baia Mare, 2000", "https://reliefweb.int/report/romania/cyanide-spill-baia-mare-romania-unepocha-assessment-mission-advance-copy"], ["ICPDR Danube Watch, the 2000 cyanide incident", "https://www.danube-iad.eu/docs/DN_articles/2000-Cyanide-Incident_mine_Baia_Mare-DanubeNews-Kalbfus.pdf"]]
properties.countries: ["Romania", "Hungary", "Hungary / Ukraine border river", "Hungary", "Serbia", "Romania / Serbia border river", "Bulgaria / Romania border river", "Romania", "Romania / Ukraine border river"]

properties.name: Benzene spill, Songhua River
properties.count_note: An explosion released about 100 t of benzene compounds. Harbin shut off its water supply from 23 November.
properties.water: The slick moved down the Songhua under forming ice, past Harbin, into the Amur (Heilongjiang) and on to Khabarovsk in Russia.
properties.place: Jilin Petrochemical plant, Jilin City, China
properties.sources: [["UNEP field mission report, December 2005", "https://archive.eecentre.org/eecentre.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/China-december-2005-UNEP-Mission-Report.pdf"], ["OCHA situation report no. 2", "https://reliefweb.int/report/china/peoples-republic-chinarussian-federation-chemical-spill-ocha-situation-report-no-2"]]
properties.countries: ["People's Republic of China", "People's Republic of China / Russia border river", "Russia"]

properties.name: Tailings dam collapse, Rio Doce
properties.count_note: 19 people died. The mud travelled 620-670 km to the Atlantic.
properties.water: Through the Gualaxo do Norte and Carmo into the Rio Doce; reached the Atlantic at Regência about 17 days later.
properties.sources: [["Marta-Almeida et al. 2016, Fund\u00e3o Dam collapse: oceanic dispersion of River Doce", "https://agris.fao.org/search/en/records/65df21bd4c5aef494fe021e9"]]

properties.name: Sandoz chemical fire, Rhine
properties.agent: Pesticides and mercury compounds in fire-fighting water
properties.count_note: Tonnes of agrochemicals washed into the Rhine with fire-fighting water from about 01:30 on 1 November 1986; mass eel kill downstream.
properties.water: The red pollution wave moved down the Rhine through Germany and the Netherlands to the North Sea. It led to the Rhine Action Programme of 1987.
properties.sources: [["Giger 2009, The Rhine red, the fish dead - the 1986 Schweizerhalle disaster", "https://doc.rero.ch/record/317970?ln=en"], ["ICPR / CHR Rhine alarm model", "https://chr-khr.org/sites/default/files/chrpublications/brochure_ram_e.pdf"]]
properties.countries: ["Germany / Switzerland border river", "France / Germany border river", "Germany", "Netherlands"]
